_comment: PROPOSED. Not the approved policy, and NOT SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN.
What counts as confidential is a business rule INZBC owns (#37), so this file is a starting
point for that decision, not a substitute for it. Nothing loads it by default:
REDACTION_POLICY_PATH is unset, so every model call still refuses until someone points it at an
approved file. Approving it means copying it to the deployment path under a name without
'proposed' in it, and recording who approved it.
LIMIT, stated plainly because it decides how this may be used: these rules match FORMATTED
IDENTIFIERS. They cannot catch a person's name, job title, employer, or anything else carried in
ordinary prose, and no regex will. 'Delegation lead: Priya Sharma, Chief Executive, Koru Exports'
passes through untouched. Review before publication does not help, because disclosure to the
model provider has already happened by then. The real control for that data is not sending it:
prohibited inputs and structured-field removal, tracked as #223.
Every rule carries an example it must actually redact, or the policy will not load. The examples
below use example.test addresses and invented numbers. Do not put real member data in this file:
it is committed to the repository.

rules.name: email
rules.example: forward it to sunil@example.test before Friday

rules.name: passport
rules.example: delegate passport LA123456 expires next year

rules.name: nz-bank-account
rules.example: deposit to 01-0123-0123456-00 by the due date

rules.name: street-address
rules.example: the office moved to 123 Queen Street last year

rules.name: credential
rules.example: the key is sk-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX and it works

rules.name: visa-or-immigration-reference
rules.example: work visa NZV123456 expires in March
